items.prompt: Why is largest-first not a correct universal minimum-coin algorithm?

options.text: For coins 1, 3, 4 and amount 6 it uses three coins while 3+3 uses two
options.why: One legal counterexample is enough to disprove universal optimality.

options.text: No greedy algorithm can ever be correct for any problem
options.why: Some have valid domain-specific exchange/proof arguments.

options.text: A unit coin makes the amount unreachable
options.why: A unit coin makes reachability easier, not optimality automatic.

options.text: All dynamic programs require exponential tables
options.why: These examples have polynomial-in-numeric-amount table work.

items.explanation: Separate feasibility from optimality. The worked coin system is a specific counterexample, not an argument against every greedy algorithm.
